captured_by: PoC implementation session, not Visit Finland curator staff
provenance: This schema and the category file were written for demonstration purposes from general domain knowledge of the Accommodation product type and typical DataHub curator concepts (found/review/missing status, evidence requirement, tri-state accessibility, category limits). They are NOT transcribed from official DataHub curator documentation and have not been confirmed against a machine-readable DataHub source.
known_gaps: Field list is a representative subset (name, description, address, coordinates, contact, categories, accessibility, sustainability_label, stf_status, capacity, pricing, booking_url, availability, opening_hours, amenities, languages_spoken, images) and is not the complete DataHub Accommodation field list.
Stable category identifiers are invented for this PoC (e.g. 'accommodation.hotel') and are not DataHub's real category identifiers.

schemas/datahub-categories.json holds ~20 entries, not DataHub's full ~200-entry taxonomy. This is a deliberate PoC-scope decision, not a placeholder pending Phase 0 transcription -- see the plan's 'Category vocabulary' section. Expanding it is out of scope for this release.
Required-versus-conditionally-required distinctions per DataHub product subtype are not encoded.
Cardinality constraints beyond the categories array are not encoded.
Deprecated values are not tracked, because no source listing them was available.
Import-specific rules that only appear in the DataHub import pipeline (not the curator UI) are unknown.

design_decisions.detail: Categories are never reported as 'found', only 'review' or 'missing'. Assigning a category id to a business is a classification/mapping judgment, not a verbatim extraction, even when the mapping is close to unambiguous. scripts/validate_extraction.py enforces this deterministically (rule_id category_is_classification) and downgrades a 'found' category to 'review' unconditionally, regardless of taxonomy completeness. This is a permanent design decision, not a provisional rule awaiting confirmation.

provisional_rules.reason: DataHub guidance to 'choose only five the most relevant categories' reads as a recommendation. Whether the import treats a sixth category as a warning or a hard error is unconfirmed.

schemas/datahub-categories.json is an intentionally small, non-authoritative PoC subset, so an unrecognized category id is at least as likely to be a gap in the subset as an invalid choice. It is a warning rather than an error regardless of taxonomy size; see scripts/validate_extraction.py.
